issues.t: High-voltage battery fire risk, charge limit to 80% (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning. Some owners have seen high-voltage battery or 'risk of fire' messages. Audi tells owners to charge only to 80% until a fix is ready.
issues.why: The high-voltage battery in certain 2024-2025 Q4 e-tron and Q4 Sportback e-tron models may fail and could start a fire. Audi is still developing the final repair.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. Set the charge limit to 80% as Audi instructs, and watch for owner letters about the free repair. If you see a battery or fire warning, stop, get out and call for help.

issues.t: Onboard charger failure drains 12-volt battery and cuts power (recall)
issues.sym: Warning messages, a car that shuts down while driving or won't start, and a 12-volt battery that keeps going flat.
issues.why: The onboard charger and DC-DC converter unit can fail and stop charging the 12-volt battery. When that battery runs down, the car can lose drive power.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall. The dealer replaces the onboard charger unit for free. If warnings appear while driving, pull over somewhere safe.

issues.t: Car shuts off while driving or won't start
issues.sym: The car suddenly loses power or shuts down while driving or stopped, may not restart for several minutes, or fails to start at random.
issues.why: Owners link it to low 12-volt battery voltage, the onboard charger recall and software faults. Dealers often can't reproduce it and fix it with software updates or a new 12-volt battery.
issues.next: Note the warnings and when it happens, and take photos of the dash. Ask the dealer to check for the onboard charger recall, software updates and the 12-volt battery.

issues.sym: When charging at home with the compact 240-volt cord, the plug, outlet or cable can get hot, smell burnt or melt, especially on long charges to 100%.
issues.why: With some home outlets, the plug end of the 240-volt portable charging cable can overheat under a long, full charge.
issues.next: Stop using the 240-volt portable cord until Audi gives you the replacement cable with a temperature sensor. Use the 120-volt cord, a wall-mounted charger or public chargers instead.

issues.t: Gear indicator may be wrong, car can roll away (recall)
issues.sym: The dash may not show the correct gear position, so you could think the car is in Park when it isn't.
issues.why: A brake control unit software fault can stop the gear indicator from displaying properly. If the parking brake isn't set, the car could roll.
issues.next: Always make sure the parking brake is on when you get out. Have the free software update done at a dealer.

issues.t: Side curtain airbag can tear on door seal (recall)
issues.sym: No symptoms. In a crash, a side curtain airbag could tear and not protect as well as it should.
issues.why: When the curtain airbag deploys, it can push the door seal out of place, and a metal piece inside the seal can tear the airbag.
issues.next: Have the free recall done. The dealer adds protective tape in the front door pillar area.

issues.sym: With the headlights on and a turn signal flashing, the parking lights may not stay lit as they should, making the car harder to see.
issues.why: The headlight control module has incorrect software.
issues.next: Have the dealer update the headlight control module for free.

issues.t: Rearview camera image blank or frozen (recall)
issues.sym: When you shift into reverse, the screen shows nothing or a frozen image instead of the camera view.
issues.why: The rearview camera itself can fail on some 2022 models.
issues.next: Check for this recall. The dealer replaces the rear camera for free. Until then, use your mirrors and look behind you.

issues.t: Charging fails or shows charging malfunction
issues.sym: The car won't charge reliably, shows a charging system malfunction message, stops charging part way, or only accepts some types of charger.
issues.why: Faults in the charge port lock actuator, the onboard charger or the charging software. Owners report a connector lock actuator replacement and software updates fixing it.
issues.next: Try another charger and cable first. If it continues, have the dealer check the charge port lock, the onboard charger recall and software updates.

issues.sym: The low-speed warning sound that alerts people walking nearby cuts in and out or doesn't play at all, including when reversing.
issues.why: A fault in the sound generator or its wiring or software. Owners report dealers finding a faulty sound system.
issues.next: Take extra care in parking lots and have the dealer fix it under warranty, since the sound is a required safety feature.

issues.t: Tires wear out early or lose tread chunks
issues.sym: Front or rear tires wear out by 10,000-20,000 miles, chunks of tread peel off, or a tire fails after a low-pressure warning.
issues.why: The heavy weight and instant torque of an EV wear tires fast. Owners report factory all-season tires losing tread chunks at low mileage.
issues.next: Check tire tread and pressures monthly, rotate tires on schedule and have the alignment checked. Ask the dealer or tire maker about warranty if tread is coming apart.

issues.t: Unexpected hard braking or parking brake engaging
issues.sym: The car brakes hard on its own at low speed, the electronic parking brake engages during slow maneuvers, or the brakes feel slow to respond.
issues.why: Owners report sudden braking events that dealers have not been able to reproduce. Driver-assist or brake control software is suspected.
issues.next: Keep notes on when it happens and report it to the dealer and to NHTSA. Ask for a check of brake control software updates.

issues.t: Keyless entry or remote lock stops working
issues.sym: The doors don't unlock with the key nearby or with the app, or remote lock and unlock works only some of the time.
issues.why: Often linked to a weak 12-volt battery; in one case a new 12-volt battery fixed it.
issues.next: Have the 12-volt battery tested and ask about the onboard charger recall.
